steps.message:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close September 30, 2026 at 5:00 PM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To convert the contest deadline to your local time in Madrid, Spain:

1. **Source Time (ET):** On September 30, 2026, the US is observing Eastern Daylight Time (EDT, UTC-4). 5:00 PM EDT is 17:00 EDT.
2. **Target Time (Madrid):** On September 30, 2026, Madrid is observing Central European Summer Time (CEST, UTC+2).
3. **Time Difference:** CEST is 6 hours ahead of EDT.
4. **Calculation:** 17:00 EDT + 6 hours = 23:00 (11:00 PM) CEST on September 30, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-09-30 23:00

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: July 15, 2026, 12:00 UTC."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Lima, Peru operates on Peru Time (PET), which is UTC-5 year-round (no daylight saving time). 

Subtracting 5 hours from 12:00 UTC on July 15, 2026 gives 07:00 on the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-07-15 07:00

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Applications are due June 1, 2026 at 9:00 AM CEST."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Central European Summer Time (CEST) is UTC+2, while Tokyo (Japan Standard Time, JST) is UTC+9. This means Tokyo is 7 hours ahead of CEST.

Adding 7 hours to June 1, 2026, at 9:00 AM CEST gives 4:00 PM (16:00) on June 1, 2026, in Tokyo time.

ANSWER: 2026-06-01 16:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The contest ends on October 11, 2026 at 11:59 PM PDT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To convert the contest deadline to your local time in Madrid, Spain:

1. **PDT (Pacific Daylight Time)** is UTC-7. On October 11, 2026, PDT is active in North America.
2. **CEST (Central European Summer Time)** in Madrid is UTC+2. On October 11, 2026, Spain is still observing Daylight Saving Time (which ends on October 25, 2026).
3. The time difference between PDT and CEST is **9 hours ahead**.

Adding 9 hours to October 11, 2026, at 11:59 PM PDT gives October 12, 2026, at 8:59 AM CEST.

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 08:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close March 3, 2026 at 11:59 PM PST."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To determine the deadline in Madrid time:

1. **Given Time:** March 3, 2026, at 11:59 PM PST (Pacific Standard Time, UTC-8).
2. **Target Location:** Madrid, Spain is in the Central European Time zone (CET, UTC+1) in early March, as Daylight Saving Time has not yet started.
3. **Time Difference:** CET is 9 hours ahead of PST (from UTC-8 to UTC+1).

Adding 9 hours to March 3, 2026, at 11:59 PM (23:59) brings the time to 8:59 AM the following morning, March 4, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-03-04 08:59

I live in Los Angeles, USA. A contest page says: "Deadline: 10:00 AM CET, February 2, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

CET (Central European Time) in February is UTC+1. 
Los Angeles is in PST (Pacific Standard Time) in February, which is UTC-8. 

This creates a 9-hour time difference (PST is 9 hours behind CET). Subtracting 9 hours from 10:00 AM on February 2, 2026, gives 1:00 AM on the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-02-02 01:00

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Submit by 8:00 AM JST on May 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Japan Standard Time (JST) is UTC+9, and Lima, Peru operates on Peru Time (PET), which is UTC-5. This means Lima is 14 hours behind JST.

Subtracting 14 hours from 8:00 AM on May 5, 2026, gives 6:00 PM on May 4, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-05-04 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 28, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To convert the deadline to your local time in Madrid, Spain:

1. **Pacific Time (PT) on October 28, 2026**: The US is still in Pacific Daylight Time (PDT, which is UTC-7), as daylight saving time ends on November 1, 2026.
2. **Madrid Time on October 28, 2026**: The EU ends daylight saving time on the last Sunday of October (October 25, 2026). Therefore, by October 28, Madrid will be in Central European Time (CET, which is UTC+1).

The difference between PDT (UTC-7) and CET (UTC+1) is **8 hours**. 

Adding 8 hours to October 28, 2026, at 11:59 PM PDT brings us to 7:59 AM the following morning in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-10-29 07:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The live session starts October 30, 2026, 9:00 AM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To convert the contest time to your local time in Madrid:

1. **Eastern Time (ET):** On October 30, 2026, the US is in Eastern Daylight Time (EDT, UTC-4) because Daylight Saving Time ends on November 1, 2026.
2. **Madrid Time:** In Spain, Daylight Saving Time ends on the last Sunday of October (October 25, 2026). Therefore, on October 30, 2026, Madrid will be on Central European Time (CET, UTC+1).
3. **Time Difference:** UTC+1 is 5 hours ahead of UTC-4.
4. **Conversion:** Adding 5 hours to 9:00 AM EDT yields 2:00 PM (14:00) CET on the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-10-30 14:00

I live in New York, USA. A contest page says: "Voting closes October 27, 2026 at 18:00 CET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To convert October 27, 2026 at 18:00 CET to your local time in New York:

1. **Central European Time (CET)** is UTC+1. (Europe switches from daylight saving time to standard time on October 25, 2026, so CET is active). 
2. **New York Time** on October 27, 2026 is Eastern Daylight Time (EDT, UTC-4), as the US daylight saving time ends on November 1, 2026.
3. The difference between CET (UTC+1) and EDT (UTC-4) is 5 hours.
4. Subtracting 5 hours from 18:00 yields 13:00 on the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-10-27 13:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Final round closes November 2, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To determine the deadline in Madrid, Spain (CET):

1. **Pacific Time (PT) on November 2, 2026:**
   - In the US, Daylight Saving Time ends on the first Sunday of November (November 1, 2026).
   - Therefore, on November 2, 2026, Pacific Time is in Pacific Standard Time (PST), which is **UTC-8**.

2. **Madrid Time (CET) on November 2, 2026:**
   - In Europe, Daylight Saving Time ends on the last Sunday of October (October 25, 2026).
   - Therefore, on November 2, 2026, Madrid is in Central European Time (CET), which is **UTC+1**.

3. **Time Difference:**
   - Madrid (UTC+1) is **9 hours ahead** of Pacific Time (UTC-8).

4. **Conversion:**
   - 11:59 PM PT on November 2, 2026 + 9 hours = **8:59 AM on November 3, 2026**.

ANSWER: 2026-11-03 08:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close March 20, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To convert the deadline to your local time in Madrid, Spain:

1. **Pacific Time (PT):** Daylight Saving Time in the US starts on March 8, 2026. Therefore, on March 20, PT is Pacific Daylight Time (PDT), which is **UTC-7**.
2. **Madrid Time:** Daylight Saving Time in Europe starts on March 29, 2026. Therefore, on March 20, Madrid is on Central European Time (CET), which is **UTC+1**.
3. **Difference:** Madrid is 8 hours ahead of Pacific Time (UTC+1 vs UTC-7).

Adding 8 hours to March 20, 2026 at 11:59 PM (23:59) PDT gives March 21, 2026 at 7:59 AM CET.

ANSWER: 2026-03-21 07:59

I live in Los Angeles, USA. A contest page says: "The webinar starts March 25, 2026, 12:00 PM CET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

On March 25, 2026, Europe has not yet switched to Daylight Saving Time (which occurs on March 29, 2026), so Central European Time (CET) is UTC+1. Meanwhile, Los Angeles will already be observing Pacific Daylight Time (PDT, UTC-7) as Daylight Saving Time in the US starts on March 8, 2026. 

The time difference between CET (UTC+1) and PDT (UTC-7) is 8 hours. Subtracting 8 hours from 12:00 PM CET gives 4:00 AM PDT on the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-03-25 04:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 12:00 AM ET on October 12, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To determine the deadline in Madrid time:

1. **Convert 12:00 AM ET on October 12, 2026:** "12:00 AM" refers to midnight at the start of the day (00:00).
2. **Check Daylight Saving Time:**
   * On October 12, 2026, the US is on Eastern Daylight Time (EDT), which is UTC-4.
   * On October 12, 2026, Madrid is on Central European Summer Time (CEST), which is UTC+2.
3. **Calculate the difference:** Madrid (UTC+2) is 6 hours ahead of Eastern Daylight Time (UTC-4).
4. **Apply the offset:** Adding 6 hours to 00:00 EDT on October 12 gives 06:00 CEST on October 12.

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 06:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Papers are due October 9, 2026 (23:59 AoE)."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To find the deadline in Madrid's local time:

1. **AoE Time Zone**: "Anywhere on Earth" (AoE) corresponds to UTC-12. 
   - October 9, 2026, at 23:59 AoE is equivalent to October 10, 2026, at 11:59 UTC.

2. **Madrid Time Zone**: On October 10, 2026, Madrid will be observing Central European Summer Time (CEST), which is UTC+2 (Daylight Saving Time ends on the last Sunday of October).

3. **Conversion**: Adding 14 hours (the difference between UTC-12 and UTC+2) to October 9, 2026, at 23:59 yields October 10, 2026, at 13:59.

ANSWER: 2026-10-10 13:59

This puts Madrid 9 hours ahead of Pacific Time. Adding 9 hours to 12:00 PM (noon) PDT on August 14, 2026 gives 21:00 (9:00 PM) CEST on the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-08-14 21:00

   * **Madrid, Spain (Central European Time in November):** Daylight Saving Time in Spain ends on October 25, 2026, so on November 10, 2026, Madrid will be observing standard Central European Time (CET), which is UTC+1.

2. **Calculate the difference:**
   * Madrid (UTC+1) is **4 hours and 30 minutes behind** IST (UTC+5:30).

3. **Subtract the offset:**
   * 11:59 PM (23:59) IST minus 4 hours and 30 minutes equals **19:29** on the same day.

3. **Time Difference**: Sydney (UTC+10) is 8 hours ahead of Madrid (UTC+2).
